text:
Sasha (Support): ping — customer ACME corp is hitting 500s from /v1/rerank during a batch job. They say the payload contains emoji and some legacy latin1 bytes, and our Node SDK retry loop charged them for 3 attempts :grimacing:. Request ids: req-54a2, req-54a3. Repro steps below.

Maya (SRE): can you paste the exact payload and the earliest request id? Also did they send Content-Encoding or any charset headers?

Sasha (Support): earliest id req-54a2. Payload (redacted) — note I replaced non-printables with \x00 to show nulls:
```json
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "query": "What is the best option?\u0000",
  "candidates": ["Option A", "Option B", "Café — café", "Emoji: 😊"]
}
```
Node SDK v1.3.2, we saw 500 with internal parser error in logs: `utf8 decoder error: unexpected continuation byte`.

Kevin (Eng-ML): :eyes: that stack sounds like our C++ tokenizer choking on embedded NUL and mixed encoding. If the tokenizer throws before token accounting completes, our handler returns 500 but the usage middleware already recorded tokens — hence the billing problem.

Paul (Billing): can we get a list of timestamps/req ids so we can issue credits? which customers affected?

Sasha (Support): ACME had two jobs across 2026-02-15T11:02:33Z (req-54a2) and 11:12:01Z (req-54a3). They processed ~12k candidate strings; the failures happened when a payload chunk contained a stray 0x00 and some ISO-8859-1 bytes that looked like `Ã©` instead of `é`.

Maya (SRE): I'll open an incident and paste logs. @eng-oncall can you take a look at the runtime decoder? Quick mitigation: we can sanitize inputs at the HTTP ingress to replace 0x00 with U+FFFD and force UTF-8 normalization. That would stop the crash and probably avoid double-counting tokens if done before usage middleware.

eng-oncall: taking. ETA 30m to triage. If we can roll a hotfix at ingress to reject+400 or sanitize, do we prefer reject? :thinking: 

Kevin (Eng-ML): Prefer sanitize with a debug flag for now. Rejecting will cause customer churn and more support tickets. Also we should add a billing rule: if status >=500 and parser exception in logs, flag for review and refund automatically.

Paul (Billing): agree on refund automation. pls add the rule and I'll prep manual credits for ACME for the two req ids.

support-bot: incident created: INC-20260215-83 — assigned to eng-oncall, severity P2.

Sasha (Support): Thanks. I'll tell ACME we're working on a sanitizer patch and will issue credits. I'll attach repro script for eng:
```bash
cat <<EOF >bad.json
{"query":"Hello\u0000","candidates":["A","B","Café","Emoji: \xF0\x9F\x98\x8A"]}
EOF
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $REPRO" -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=binary" \ 
  --data-binary @bad.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank
```

Kevin (Eng-ML): got it. I'll try reproducing with Node v1.3.2 and libtokenizer 2.0. If I can repro locally I'll bench sanitizer patch and push to prod canary.

Maya (SRE): tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml. Closing loop: Sasha, please paste any customer logs you get from ACME after you inform them. :thumbsup:

Sasha (Support): will do. ACME is on standby, they're worried about billing. Paul, sending invoice refs now.

Paul (Billing): received. Preparing credits. :money_with_wings:

Kevin (Eng-ML): quick note — also add a test to our fuzz harness for embedded NUL + ISO-8859-1 sequences to catch regressions.

Sasha (Support): thanks team :heart:
